messages:
maria: seeing GPU attach failures in ap-southeast1 since ~13:24 UTC. Autoscaler shows nodes stuck in PROVISIONING with error 'device setup timeout'. iostat shows local NVMe qdepth 95%+ across scratchpool nodes. Noticed large scrub activity kicked off around 13:20 UTC. repeating errors: 

infra-bot: ALERT: nvme_io_throttle_high on node-group scratchpool-ap-southeast1 (13:25:18 UTC). link: https://monitoring.redwood.internal/alerts/7421

kevin: yep scrub job started for overlay cleanup across zones at 13:19. bad overlap with scheduled batch ramp. we throttle scrubs normally but looks like the sampler hit a high-concurrency path.

samir: can we pause scrub on one AZ to free up iops for provisioning? quick mitigation = suspend cron for scrub-nightly in ap-southeast1. longer term = move scrub window off peak.

eli: agree. immediate steps: 1) throttle scrub rate 2) suspend cron in problematic AZs 3) backfill cleanup later during low-traffic window. I can run the commands if we agree.

kevin: i can throttle now. patching env var to reduce concurrency from 8 -> 2 and restarting. command i'm using: 

```
kubectl -n infra set env daemonset/ephemeral-scrubber SCRUB_CONCURRENCY=2
kubectl -n infra rollout restart daemonset/ephemeral-scrubber
```

kevin: rolling out to ap-southeast1 only (label selector) to avoid global impact. should take ~90s per nodegrp.

maria: good. also let's suspend the cron for zone-a only as backup: 

```
kubectl -n infra patch cronjob scrub-nightly -p '{"spec":{"suspend":true}}' --context=cluster-apse-zone-a
```

sre-oncall: temporary mitigation looks fine. note: if we suspend too long backlog grows and increases wear when it runs again. we should document the new window before re-enabling. open runbook ticket.

ops-runbook-bot: Runbook: NVMe IO overload during scrub/cleanup - https://redwood.internal/runbooks/nvme-io. Recommended actions: throttle SCRUB_CONCURRENCY, suspend cron for affected AZ, consider shifting to 00:30 UTC window, monitor nvme_io_throttle_high and gpu_attach_fail metrics.

samir: i'll create a quick ticket to shift the window to 00:30 UTC for ap-southeast1 and call out cost/wear tradeoffs. backlog estimate if we delay 6h = ~120k files to scrub, will take longer with lower concurrency.

maria: for capacity routing, if provisioning still fails after scrub throttle we can temporarily route new GPU requests to us-west2 via the autoscaler policy override. that costs ~+$0.60/instance-hour vs waiting, but keeps customer jobs alive. ops note: prefer not to move live workloads unless necessary.

kevin: throttle applied. initial metric check: nvme qdepth dropped from 95% -> 62% in 3 minutes. gpu attach failures stopped in the last 2 samples. monitoring tail: https://monitoring.redwood.internal/d/xyz/ephemeral-io?orgId=1

eli: i'll keep an eye for 30m and then we can re-enable cron for zone-a with lower concurrency. if metrics re-spike we keep it suspended and escalate to firmware-level investigation.

maria: action items: kevin = keep scrub concurrency=2 in ap-southeast1 for now and post final rollback plan; samir = create schedule-change ticket + update runbook; eli = monitor and report at +30m; sre-oncall = stand by for autoscaler routing decision.

kevin: noted. i'll post the rollout id once the daemonset finishes.

eli: +1. will notify customer-facing teams if we need cross-region routing.

maria: thanks all. we'll reconvene if repro shows up again.
